items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: Who gets off the train? ... Mike Lyman. ... He comes, man, where you going? I said, man, I'm just sick to go get it. Tickets that Joe sent for me.

ctx.x: And he sent me a ticket. This is after he went to New York? After he went back, yeah. He sent it for me. That's when he had this big band we were going to have down there and all that bunch of plays for him. He sent it for me. I goes to work like a fool and so much to do the bank.

And so much to do the bank. And that same day, just as the man gave me the money from my car and I was out of the 60th Street to the station to get this ticket, you see. Who gets off the train? I had a train. I said, Because she was on the train. I don't know what made me stop and go look out on the platform. He'll come over it. Where was she coming from? Oh. Coming from up here. Mike Lyman. Yeah. He had a, uh, at, uh, at, uh, at, uh, at, uh, at the, uh, at the, uh, at the, uh, at the Oakland Oakland Oakland…

Ed Garland, April 16, 1957, Rule 4. I said, come on. So we're going to bust them all back down there. I don't go there and tell the man. I don't tell you the ticket down yet now. I go back to the man. I say, I'm sorry. I says, the order just come for me, and I'm not going away. I says, I'd like to redeem your car, give me money back. I said, you can't give me that money back. You can't put $100 to give it back to me. I said, oh man, I'm sorry. You got your money and the receipt. I got the receipt. Well, I'm going…
